# Catharisism
## 1
What do you call a person who heals by working hard? Not exactly a "workaholic" but closer to; hermit + empath/HSP + any of (polymath, brilliance, genius, talent, creativity). Bordering between Savant + Socially dysfunctional - and - Functional Autism/Depression.

Thus... One may even infer, such a person uses Work, Academia or Engagement, almost as a Cathartic Catalyst to express what is otherwise inexpressibe in everyday waking life. I think a "Catharsian", "Catharstician" or "Catharthisist" is perhaps the closest non-typical wording to describe this Phenomenology...becuase not only do these words combine "Catharsis" which is the central root emotion, but they also emphasize the role of the Profession and Professional; i.e., "ist", "ician", or "isist" are common suffixes in this case.

The most common Physiological Phenomenology one may describe, at peak moments of the "Catharisist" is "Enthusiasm", and likewise, the depressive-like symptoms afformetioned, would most likely summarize into a complete opposite: "Apathy." This is, honestly, the primary tragedy for the Catharisist... prologned states of Apathy directly inspired me to research this word to begin with... however, the personal Phenomenology is a topic for another discussion.

When such a person is not working (or engaged in their necessary, natural enviornment) for prolonged periods of time, they exhibit symptoms devoid of aliveness (psychological exhaustion, depletion, apathy, etc.). What may such a person be called? I propose "Catharsisist" and variations, truly hit the nail on the head, which is a complex task, considering the manifold nature of this particular Human Trait... it isn't very well documented or even understood... other than the common stereotypes: "The isolated genius" or "Polymath's and Brilliant people are just not very well socialized."

Does Psychology recognize this Empirically? Not as a "DSM-5" criterion, as this is most likely a personality/temperament trait... not a bookshelf disorder...

Below is the second half of the story.

## 2
If a single word could describe the Human Condtiion... such that Suffering itself is part of something meaningful requiring it.

"The conditions of life are alike to War... if not externally, the internal war never ceases. So then, if the default conditions of life are push-and-pull, what sustains oneself in battle? It appears that the work itself must be intrinsically meaningful... and this sustains oneself... for 'Man cannot live by bread alone.'"

Let's research Orthogonal Greek words for the opening dramatic description of this word... a sort of "Tangible, Tactile Telos..."

"One is devoid of life and meaning when living as a machine, an automata. Living for responsibilities of the modern life. When the Call of Duty has been replaced by the Call of the Void (philosophical reference...), one must find that which splits the edge between waking life and the dormant soul-draining path of the world outside. Perhaps, reclusing, or becoming a Hermit for a season or two, is not entirely mad. For the world we live in is terribly complex, and it demands careful analysis and understanding. In the busy hustle of the world outside, one's internal moral compass is finely tuned when Educated; not merely to 'Know Thyself' but to Live correctly; however one may come to understand it; it is a collective, decentralized tuning, much like the magnetism of North; the direction of one's life cannot be determined by..."

This word combines two distinct concepts:

- Alpha and Creation: "In the beginning, the only thing that allows one to begin is as the Logos of the Christian tradition; a decision to speak forth Good in Creation." The Human being has something within that generates natural momentum to endure, persist and push forward. We can distinctly define this as "Sisyphus-ian Enthusiasm." This includes our ability to create and speak, and express with the voice. Creativity, not as Automata-production, but as the Creative force which brings order out of Potentiality and Entropy.
    
- Omega and Telos: A relentless Torrent of Enthusiasm, bordering on Delirum, Berserk and Mania, but with the Conscious control of Awareness; A form of "Applied Enthusiasm."
    

In it's essence, this word captures the very heart of the Human being atleast, for those individuals who see beyond the everyday Facade; realize the Facade is necessary; and choose to build and construct and study and become, despite insufficient resources or constraints.

It captures the "War-like" essence of pursuit; but it must be tethered within a proper Telos. IT's essentially; that which gives life to the Human-Being; and without it, the Human-Being is merely a Human

Even more interestingly; the word fuses these distant halves to form a whole; both the Telos and the Creation are necessarily Incomplete; To pursue a Telos, is to Create and Build and Become... for one is yet fundamentally in the process of "Becoming"... and that requires Enthusiasm and Inherit meaning...which is precisely why it is so important to emphasize the act of tactile craft; or in Aristotle's terms "Techne, Phronesis, Praxis and Sophia"

Ultimately, the second-half of "Human" is "Being", and part of "Being" is paradoxically not found in the "Momentary Ontology of Being" but "What one was, and what one is to become." That is essential to the "Alpha and Creation" Portion of the Etymology. The second half, emphasizes

Essentially the word would resemble a "dictionary of obscure sorrows"-esque + Greek-etymological essence which feels timeless...
